name: Joe Becker (Unicode)
milestone_by_age_26: No confirmed birth year in reviewed sources; career-defining Unicode work (Unicode 88 paper 1988; consortium leadership) came in the 1980s after a Stanford PhD (1970) and Xerox PARC career (from 1977). Without birth year, age-26 eligibility cannot be established for earlier work.
early_history_summary: Joseph D. Becker earned a BS in Mathematics from MIT (1966) and a PhD in Computer Science from Stanford (1970). After joining Xerox PARC (1977) he worked on multilingual office systems, co-founded the Unicode effort with Lee Collins and Mark Davis in the late 1980s, and coined the term Unicode.
evidence_summary: Unicode Consortium leadership bios document MIT BS 1966 and Stanford PhD 1970 but not birth year. Seminal multilingual work and Unicode 88 are mid/late-career standards efforts, not verifiable age-≤26 milestones. Wikipedia marks year of birth missing.

name: Larry Constantine
milestone_by_age_26: By 1968 at age 25, substantially completed the core of structured design—including structure charts and coupling/cohesion metrics—presented at the National Symposium on Modular Programming, and joined the faculty of IBM’s Systems Research Institute.
early_history_summary: Born 1943 in Anoka, Minnesota; graduated Anoka High School 1961; programmed at MIT Laboratory for Nuclear Science (1963) and CEIR (1963–66) while studying at MIT Sloan (S.B. management 1967). Founded/led Information & Systems Institute (1966–68) and taught at Wharton as an undergraduate; modular programming and structured design ideas crystallized by 1968.
family_context_summary: Raised in Anoka, Minnesota; mother Loraine Constantine worked as a local newspaper editor/columnist in the 1950s. Broader family wealth and father occupation not richly documented in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother’s journalism work is documented; no clear parental software-engineering apprenticeship path in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: MIT Sloan, MIT Lab Nuclear Science, IBM Systems Research Institute, early modular programming community, CEIR consulting
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and computing-pioneer references place birth on 14 Feb 1943 and state structured design’s core (structure charts, coupling/cohesion) was substantially complete by 1968 when Constantine was 25, including National Symposium on Modular Programming presentation and IBM SRI faculty role. Earlier MIT/CEIR programming and Information & Systems Institute presidency (from ~age 23) show sustained reps. Family domain advantage is weak; MIT pipeline and early computer access are the clearest documented early conditions. Later Structured Design book with Yourdon (1975) and usage-centered design cemented tier-2 historical status.
starting_point: Born 1943 in Anoka, Minnesota; Midwestern high-school path into MIT Sloan; mother was a local newspaper editor/columnist.
current_position: Software engineering pioneer and ACM Fellow; longtime principal at Constantine & Lockwood; former professor at University of Madeira / Madeira Interactive Technologies Institute; also publishes fiction as Lior Samson.

trajectory.event: Began professional programming as technical aid at MIT Laboratory for Nuclear Science and at CEIR.
Became president of Information & Systems Institute while still finishing MIT studies.
Presented core structured design / modular programming ideas and joined IBM Systems Research Institute faculty.
Published Structured Design with Ed Yourdon, codifying coupling, cohesion, and structure charts for industry practice.
Published Software for Use with Lucy Lockwood and received a Jolt Award for usage-centered design.
Named an ACM Fellow for contributions to software engineering and human-centered design.
Received the Stevens Award for outstanding contributions to software and systems development methods.

name: Martin Eberhard

family_context_summary: Grew up in Kensington (Berkeley Hills), California. Parental occupations/wealth not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Britannica confirms birth 15 May 1960. Strict ≤26 rule: NCD in calendar 1987 is mostly after he turned 27; Tesla and Rocket eBook are well after 26. Pre-26 path is strong education and employment, not a verified founder/breakout milestone.
